threat: Malware (non-ransomware: info-stealers, RATs, wipers)
description:
Non-ransomware malware impacting endpoints, servers, or SaaS-integrated hosts. Includes information stealers, remote access trojans (RATs), loaders, banking trojans, worms, and wipers. Excludes ransomware (tracked separately).

Primary impacts:

Credential/session theft, data exfiltration, persistence and lateral movement, business email compromise enablement, command-and-control, destructive activity (non-encrypting).

Likely vectors:

Phishing and malspam, drive-by downloads, compromised sites, malvertising, supply-chain (signed-but-malicious or trojaned updates), removable media, weak controls.

Relationships:

Often enabled by Social Engineering. Credential Theft/Account Compromise may be a downstream effect.

This threat is primarily mitigated by supporting controls including ECM4, IAM1, VM1, VM3, ECM8, CNS6, BCIM1, and BCIM3.
rationale:
Remediation plan

Deploy and centrally manage malware prevention and detection capabilities across endpoints and servers, including behavioral protection, quarantine, and alerting, aligned to ECM4.
Harden endpoints and administrative systems using secure configuration baselines, script and macro restrictions, least privilege, and approved software controls, supported by IAM1 and ECM8.
Reduce exploitability through timely patching, vulnerability scanning, remediation tracking, and exception handling under VM1 and VM3.
Improve email, browser, and identity protections to reduce initial compromise opportunities and credential theft pathways.
Centralize security telemetry and monitoring for malware indicators, suspicious process behavior, lateral movement, privilege escalation, and outbound command-and-control activity under CNS6.
Define triage, containment, eradication, and recovery steps in incident runbooks and ensure prompt reporting under BCIM1 and BCIM3.
Validate backup coverage and recovery procedures for systems and data that may be damaged or altered by malware activity.
Conduct lessons-learned reviews after incidents and tune controls, blocklists, detection logic, and user guidance accordingly.

threat: Application and API Exploitation (public-facing and internal, incl. unpatched systems)
description:
Attackers exploit vulnerabilities or weak configurations in applications, services, APIs, integrations, or underlying components (including libraries/dependencies and unpatched systems) across both internet-exposed and internal/partner-connected environments. Outcomes include unauthorized access, data exfiltration, business process manipulation, service disruption, and pivoting into connected systems and cloud services.

Scope:

Public-facing web apps, portals, and APIs (internet-exposed)Internal or partner-connected apps/APIs and components (non-public)Unpatched OS, middleware, frameworks, and third-party components/dependenciesIntegration failures or insecure patterns enabling injection, IDOR, auth/z bypass, SSRF, deserialization, supply chain flaws, etc.

Key vectors:

Known and zero-day CVEs, dependency issues (e.g., vulnerable libraries, packages)Misconfigurations (authn/authz, CORS, headers, TLS, rate limiting)Logic and access control flaws, injection (SQLi, NoSQLi), XSS, CSRF, RCE, path traversalAPI-specific issues (broken object/property level auth, mass assignment)

Social Engineering may precede exploitation (credential harvesting)Credential Theft can amplify impact (privileged access)Backup/Recovery Failure can worsen outage duration post-incident
rationale:

Detect: Centralized logging, runtime protection (RASP/WAF/WAF-as-a-service), anomaly detection, cloud/app telemetry, alerting for authz failures and suspicious patterns.
Respond: App/API incident playbooks, rollback/feature flags, hotfix/virtual patch, customer comms, forensics, token/secret rotation, regulator notifications as required.
Recover: Tested rollback and redeploy pipelines, validated backups of configs and data, resilience patterns (graceful degradation, circuit breakers), post-incident RCAs feeding back into SDLC.
notes:

Build: SAST/DAST/IAST, dependency management (e.g., Dependabot/Renovate), container scanning, IaC scanning, SBOM, signed artifacts, secrets mgmt (vault), least privilege for CI/CD.Run: WAF/API gateway with rate limiting and schema validation, patch/vuln mgmt SLAs, config baselines, hardening guides, TLS everywhere, logging and monitoring, anomaly detection.
